units.title: The map describes the invoice path at commit a41c9e2 only
units.claim: The map covers the invoice path of the Ledgerline billing service as of commit a41c9e2; refunds, dunning and the customer portal are out of scope.
units.explanation: The version and the scope bound every other statement: a reader must know which code the map describes.

omission.reason: Without the commit the map can't be checked against the code.

units.title: Five modules make up the invoice path, each behind its own index file
units.claim: billing/invoices holds the entry point, draft type and invoice write; billing/usage builds usage lines; billing/pricing prices them; billing/tax wraps the external tax provider; billing/events publishes billing events. Each module exposes its functions through its own index.ts, and modules import each other only through those files.
units.explanation: The module-level (HLD) view that the component diagram refines. Verified by reading the imports.

omission.reason: The module-to-path mapping is what a newcomer navigates by.

units.title: generateInvoice is the entry point, in billing/invoices/generate.ts lines 12–58
units.claim: The code defines generateInvoice(accountId, period) in billing/invoices/generate.ts, lines 12–58; it is the file's only exported function, and the admin Regenerate invoice action calls it from billing/admin/regenerate.ts.
units.explanation: A verified code fact: component-to-file and component-to-symbol mapping with a line range.

paraphrase.note: Path, symbol and line range stay exact.

units.title: generateInvoice calls usage, pricing and tax in a fixed order, then writes and publishes
units.claim: generateInvoice first calls collectUsage, then priceUsage, then TaxClient.quote, adds the returned tax to the draft, writes the invoice and finally publishes an event.
units.explanation: The verified call edges and their order. Each becomes a labelled calls arrow from the entry point.
mustPreserve: the order: usage, then pricing, then tax, then write, then publish

units.title: collectUsage reads usage_events and writes nothing
units.claim: collectUsage(accountId, period) in billing/usage/collect.ts reads the usage_events table (the account's rows whose occurred_at is in the period, skipping is_test events), groups them by meter into usage lines, and writes to no table.
units.explanation: A verified component with a read edge whose direction matters: the function reads the table, never the reverse.

units.title: priceUsage reads price_plans through loadPlan and prices in integer cents
units.claim: priceUsage(lines, plan) in billing/pricing/priceUsage.ts reads the price_plans table through loadPlan(planId) and multiplies each line's quantity by the plan's unit price; prices are integer cents, never floating point.
units.explanation: A verified component with a verified read edge.

units.title: priceUsage probably reads the discounts table (unconfirmed)
units.claim: priceUsage probably also reads the discounts table: the file imports discountFor, but no call site was found and the read is unconfirmed.
units.explanation: The author's inference from an import. It may be drawn only as an unconfirmed link (hedged label) or written as unconfirmed on the pricing card; never as a plain 'reads'.

paraphrase.note: The hedge must survive any rewording.

omission.reason: Dropping it hides a possible dependency; asserting it invents one. It must appear, hedged.

review.reason: Inferred relationship; the author asks for it to be traced.

units.title: TaxClient.quote calls Taxwell over HTTPS with an 8-second timeout
units.claim: TaxClient.quote(draft) in billing/tax/client.ts sends the draft to the external tax provider Taxwell over HTTPS with an 8 seconds timeout (line 21), and returns a tax amount per line that generateInvoice adds to the draft.
units.explanation: A verified component with a call edge to an external system.

units.title: Taxwell is the external tax provider, keyed by TAXWELL_API_KEY
units.claim: Taxwell is the external tax provider that TaxClient.quote calls over HTTPS; its API key is read from the TAXWELL_API_KEY environment variable when the client is constructed.
units.explanation: The external system at the end of the tax call.

units.title: Tax provider retry behaviour is unknown
units.claim: How retries work for the tax provider is not documented: TaxClient.quote has no retry code, and whether callers or the Taxwell library retry, and what happens to an invoice when a quote times out, is unknown.
units.explanation: An explicit unknown that qualifies the tax client. It stays on the tax client's card, marked unknown, and is never replaced by a plausible retry policy.

omission.reason: An unknown left out reads as 'nothing to worry about'; one filled in is invented.

units.title: The invoice and its lines are written in one transaction (generate.ts lines 44–52)
units.claim: generateInvoice writes the invoice to the invoices and invoice_lines tables inside one database transaction in billing/invoices/generate.ts, lines 44–52; if either insert fails, neither row is kept, and the invoices row is always written with status finalized.
units.explanation: A verified write edge with its all-or-nothing condition (LLD detail).

units.title: After the commit, publishInvoiceFinalized publishes invoice.finalized
units.claim: After the transaction commits, generateInvoice calls publishInvoiceFinalized(invoice) in billing/events/publish.ts, which publishes an invoice.finalized message to the billing-events topic.
units.explanation: A verified call and publish edge, ordered after the commit.

units.title: billing-events carries invoice.finalized to payment and email
units.claim: The billing-events topic receives invoice.finalized messages; the payment and email services subscribe to it, but their code was not read.
units.explanation: The message bus at the end of the path. The subscribers are named but unread, so they are not drawn as verified components.

units.title: What happens when publishing fails is unknown
units.claim: If publishing fails after the commit, the code logs the error and returns, so an invoice can exist without its event; no re-send job was found and whether one is planned is unknown.
units.explanation: An explicit unknown on the publish step, qualifying ku.publish.
mustPreserve: invoice can exist without its event

units.title: InvoiceDraft is the contract passed between the steps
units.claim: InvoiceDraft (billing/invoices/types.ts) has accountId, period, lines, subtotalCents and an optional taxCents that stays undefined until TaxClient.quote returns; BillingPeriod and PricedLine were not read.
units.explanation: The one LLD detail the source gives as code. Shown as a code element, with the types the author did not read left unexplained.

omission.reason: It is the only low-level contract in the source.

units.title: In the author's reading, billing/pricing is the pricing boundary (not enforced)
units.claim: The author reads billing/pricing as the pricing boundary, since no code outside it was seen reading price_plans; this is an interpretation, not a rule the code enforces.
units.explanation: Architectural interpretation, distinct from the verified facts. The 'not enforced' qualifier belongs to it.

review.reason: Stated by the source, but as the author's interpretation rather than a code fact.

units.title: generateInvoice reads as an orchestrator
units.claim: In the author's reading, generateInvoice behaves like an orchestrator: it holds no pricing or tax logic and only sequences the calls.
units.explanation: A second interpretation; supporting.

omission.reason: Follows from the call sequence; may be folded into it if marked as a reading.

units.title: What triggers the monthly run is unknown
units.claim: The scheduler that calls generateInvoice for every account each month was not found; only the admin action is known.
units.explanation: An open question. No scheduler, cron path or trigger may be invented.

units.title: No owner is listed for billing-events
units.claim: Who owns the billing-events topic is unknown; no owner is listed in the repository.
units.explanation: An open question.

units.title: Why invoices has a status column is unknown
units.claim: Every invoices row is written as finalized, so the purpose of the status column is unknown; it may be reserved for drafts.
units.explanation: A minor open question; the 'may be' is the author's guess.

units.title: The verified path is a fixed sequence; discounts and tax retries are not verified
units.claim: The verified invoice path is collect usage, price, quote tax, write both invoice tables in one transaction, then publish invoice.finalized; the discounts read is only probable and the tax provider's retry behaviour is unknown.
units.explanation: The takeaway, carrying its own uncertainty.

mustNotClaim.claim: TaxClient.quote retries failed requests (for example 3 times with exponential backoff).
mustNotClaim.why: The source says retry behaviour is not documented and quote has no retry code.
The source only says probably; the call site was not found.

mustNotClaim.claim: usage_events reads from (or calls) collectUsage, or collectUsage writes usage_events.
mustNotClaim.why: The read runs from collectUsage to the table, and collectUsage writes nothing.

mustNotClaim.claim: The code enforces billing/pricing as the pricing boundary.
mustNotClaim.why: The source calls this an interpretation that nothing enforces.

mustNotClaim.claim: A scheduler or cron job at a named path (e.g. billing/jobs/…) triggers the monthly run.
mustNotClaim.why: The scheduler was not found; no such path is stated.

mustNotClaim.claim: Missed invoice.finalized events are re-sent by a recovery job.
